content.thinking:
I need to fix the root cause so it doesn't name the revision, and describe each affected row on its own. The change removed the update of the stored month total from record_purchase, so a current-month purchase no longer moves it, and the other write path doesn't move it either. The statement's rendering and comparison code still read that field directly.

I'm checking the chain step and the "takings held" point, since customer loss counts as an impact, so I'd rather not name it there and instead say that no one using the shop was seen to hit a failure, with the spend-integrity check finding the problem instead.

action_items.item: Correct the stored month totals of the affected accounts once a fixed or rolled-back revision is running, for example with the repair script Code-Fix proposed: run it with --apply on an account export taken in the same month, then load the corrected accounts back.
Run the spend-integrity reconciliation (reconcile_monthly_totals) much more often than its current cadence.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call paging rotation for io-shop.
Make the io-shop deploy pipeline require the test suite to pass before any revision is deployed.
Add a review checklist rule: a change that stops writing a stored field must list every user of that field and show each one no longer depends on it.

causal_chain.step: No one using the shop was seen to hit a failure. What was seen instead: the spend-integrity check found that shoppers' stored month totals did not match the purchases behind them.

Purchases written after the onset were stored without moving the account's month total. At the revision that ran, record_purchase and record_purchase_deriving_the_month both append the purchase and add only to total_cents, so total_this_month_cents stayed where it was whichever path the purchase took.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after P2 at {P2.1}, so the service did no harm while P1's revision was running.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the window read before the onset.

causal_chain.step: That write path arrived with deploy P2 at {P2.1}, which removed the month-total update from record_purchase. All {T10.2} replicas were running that revision as of {T10.1}.

The change stopped writing total_this_month_cents, but the field was kept and the code around it still uses the stored value: the monthly statement reads it in render_monthly_statement and _compared_with_usual, the_mean_purchase_this_month and average_spend_per_item_this_month divide it by a count of purchases, and reconcile_monthly_totals compares it with the sum of the current-month purchases.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change stopped the shop from updating each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure when they bought something, while the parts of the shop that show and check that figure still use the saved copy.

contributing_factors.factor: Month-total drift was watched only by the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The module itself says nothing in the write path notices when a total and the purchases disagree.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A reconciliation run much more often, or a check at write time, would have caught the drift soon after the deploy, before most of the affected purchases were written.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call person would have been asked straight away to take the rollback Argus left for a person, rather than it waiting.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: By Code-Fix's reading, the test file at the deployed revision holds a test that pins record_purchase adding to the month total, which the deployed code no longer does. No test run before the deploy was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A required test run would likely have failed on the change and stopped it before it reached production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: No review was seen that checked who still uses total_this_month_cents before the change stopped writing it, even though the module's own docstring warns that a write moving one copy and not the other leaves two answers.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A reviewer listing the field's users would have seen that the statement, summary and reconciliation code still use the stored value, and stopped the change.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the rollout state and found every replica running the revision deployed just before the onset.
The Investigator Agent read that deployment's diff, which showed the month-total update taken out of record_purchase.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else before the onset, ruling out a flag flip.
Argus declined to roll back when nothing could tell it whether the rollback worked, and left the rollback for a person instead.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request, with tests and a one-off repair script.

input.root_cause: The change took the total_this_month_cents update out of record_purchase, and the other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, does not move it either, so every current-month purchase written afterwards left the stored month total short by its price. The field still sits on the account and is still used: render_monthly_statement and _compared_with_usual read it, the_mean_purchase_this_month and average_spend_per_item_this_month divide it by a count of purchases, and reconcile_monthly_totals compares it with the sum of the current-month purchases.
input.still_at_risk: The month totals already saved short stayed wrong, and each new purchase this month could leave them further short, so monthly statements and spend summaries could keep showing shoppers figures that disagree with what they bought; a shopper routed through the month-deriving write path could see the same drift even after a rollback.
input.symptom: Shoppers saw no failure, but their stored monthly spend totals stopped matching their purchases
